big_idea: Apply DECODING to read short sentences with CVC words.
learning_intention: We are learning to decode CVC words in a sentence.
student_learning_goal: I can decode CVC words in a sentence.
success_criteria: I can READ each CVC word in a sentence.
I can READ from left to right.
I can KEEP GOING when I meet a word I do not know.
I can RE-READ to make sense.
lesson_specific_materials: Decodable Sentence Strips (6 strips, written in marker on card stock)
Picture cards for any tricky-to-illustrate sentence words (cat, dog, sun, mat, pin, cup)

minds_on.hook: Sounder + Blendy: Today we put words into SENTENCES. Read each word. Keep going!
minds_on.teacher_script:
Both characters at the carpet. 'Reader friends — yesterday we blended one word at a time. Today we read SENTENCES with many CVC words. We DECODE each word, then keep going.'

Define. 'DECODE means use letter-sounds to read a word.'

Show Decodable Sentence Strip 1: 'The cat sat on a mat.' (Note: 'the', 'on', 'a' are common heart words — say them quickly; CVC words get decoded.)

Demo. 'Watch me read. Use the pointer. Tap each word.' Tap THE — say 'the' (heart word). Tap CAT — sound /c/-/a/-/t/ → CAT. Tap SAT — /s/-/a/-/t/ → SAT. Tap ON — say 'on' (heart word). Tap A — say 'a'. Tap MAT — /m/-/a/-/t/ → MAT.

Re-read smoothly. 'The cat sat on a mat.'

'Sounder says — sound out the CVC words. Quick-read the heart words. Re-read the whole sentence to make sense.'

Introduce 'keep going'. 'If I meet a word I don't know, I sound it out. Even if it's slow, I keep going. I do NOT stop.'

Demo Sentence 2: 'Pat the dog.' Tap PAT — /p/-/a/-/t/ → PAT. Tap THE. Tap DOG — /d/-/o/-/g/ → DOG. Re-read.

'Blendy says — re-read makes the sentence make sense. First decode, then re-read smoothly.'

Class reads Sentence 3 together. 'A pig in a hat.' Each child taps along on the air with a finger.

Close. 'Sounder + Blendy say — DECODE each word, keep going, then RE-READ.'
student_actions: Watch Sounder + Blendy demo on Strip 1
Practice 'keep going' with 1 unknown CVC word

steps.instruction: Hand each pair 6 sentence strips and 1 pointer.
For each strip, pairs take turns: one points and reads, the other listens and helps if needed. Then re-read smoothly together.
After all 6 strips, pairs pick their favourite sentence and read it once more, smoothly.
steps.teacher_prompt: Say: 'Pick a favourite. Read it smooth.'

steps.instruction: Stretch: pairs add ONE word to a sentence (write it on a sticky note) and re-read.

steps.teacher_prompt: Stop at each pair. Listen for keep-going behaviour, not stopping at unknowns.

differentiation.for_emerging: Use 3 strips only. Teacher reads heart words; child decodes only CVC words.
differentiation.for_extending: Pairs write a NEW sentence using 3 words from prior lessons.
differentiation.for_ell_or_iep: Picture cards available for any noun in the sentence.
differentiation.for_movement_learners: Stand up. Take one step per word. Read while walking.

formative_check.what_to_look_for: Five signals: tracks word by word; decodes each CVC word; quick-reads heart words; keeps going at unknowns; re-reads for sense.

discussion_prompts: What did you do when you met a tricky word?
What is your favourite sentence today?
consolidation.exit_routine: Each child reads ONE sentence aloud. Class chants 'HOO knows the sounds? YOU do!'

assessment_in_this_lesson.rationale: Lesson 4 captures B2.3 decoding in connected text.

expanded_walkthrough.title: When the child STOPS at an unknown word and waits — repairing the freeze trap at Grade 1
expanded_walkthrough.rationale: Common Grade-1 trap on B2.3: child reads three words fluently, hits an unknown CVC word, freezes, looks up at the teacher, and stops. The reader has the decoding skill but lacks the persistence to apply it under sentence-level pressure. This is a metacognitive gap, not a phonics gap.
expanded_walkthrough.setup: Sentence reading. Child reads 'The pig sat on a' fluently, then stops at MAP (or any unknown CVC word) and looks up.
expanded_walkthrough.teacher_script:
Crouch. 'Sounder asks — keep going! Sound it out. /m/... /a/... /p/... slide.'

Probe. 'You know how to do this. Sound, sound, sound, slide. You read it on the worksheet yesterday.'

Generalise. 'Sounder + Blendy say — when you meet a tricky word, you do NOT stop. You sound it out. You keep going. Then re-read the whole sentence.'

If the child resists: model once. Sound /m/-/a/-/p/ → MAP yourself, then ask the child to repeat the whole sentence.

The goal is not perfection on first read — it is the BEHAVIOUR of attempting and re-reading.
expected_student_responses: (Stretched) Sounds, continues, then RE-READS smoothly without prompt
common_misconceptions: Unknown word means stop. (Repair: keep going, sound it out.)
Wait for the teacher to say it. (Repair: try first.)
recovery_moves: Tap the first letter and say its sound: '/m/'. Wait for the child to continue.
Cover all but the first letter; uncover one at a time as the child sounds.
Praise the attempt, not the speed: 'Good — you tried. Now re-read the whole sentence.'
If still frozen, model once and have the child re-read after.

worksheet_brief.purpose: Independent practice of decoding CVC words in short sentences.

parts_outline.task: Read 3 short sentences and circle the CVC words you decoded.
Match each sentence to a picture: 3 sentences, 3 picture choices, draw a line.
Fill in the blank: 2 sentences with one CVC word missing. Choose from a word bank.
